t: The Lunda Empire was a tributary state of the Central African savanna, ruled by a sacred king titled the Mwaant Yaav.
Positional succession and perpetual kinship let it absorb chiefdoms without removing their rulers, linking the interior to Atlantic trade.
Succession disputes, the rise of the Chokwe and colonial partition in the 1890s broke it up, though the Mwaant Yaav title survives.
dyk: Under perpetual kinship, a new Lunda office-holder inherited his predecessor's identity and relationships, so ties between chiefdoms could last for generations unchanged.
ev: Tradition: Luba hunter-prince Chibinda Ilunga marries the Lunda heiress Lueji, bringing sacred kingship
Mwaant Yaav I, traditionally Naweej I, rules a regional power from the royal musumba
An eastern expedition founds the kingdom of Kazembe on the Luapula River
The Chokwe, armed through the rubber, wax and ivory trades, overrun the Lunda capital
Lunda lands are partitioned between the Congo Free State, Portuguese Angola and Northern Rhodesia
